security_audit.summary: The static external command findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences and inline role names, not executable Ruby or shell behavior. The hardcoded URL findings are documentation placeholders for Azure Web PubSub endpoints. One medium semantic issue remains because the token example prints a generated client access URL, which can expose temporary credentials through logs.

remediation.issue: Client access URL is printed to standard output in the token example.
remediation.suggestion: Do not log token.getUrl() or generated access tokens. Log only non-sensitive metadata, or redact token query parameters before diagnostics.

semantic_findings.title: Client Access Token Printed to Logs
semantic_findings.description: The example prints a generated client access URL to standard output. These URLs can contain temporary credentials, so copying the pattern can expose tokens in application logs.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The example directly prints token.getUrl() after generating a client access token. Azure Web PubSub client access URLs commonly include authentication material, making log exposure a realistic risk.

content.user_title: Build Azure Web PubSub Java Apps
content.value_statement: Real-time Java services need reliable WebSocket messaging patterns. This skill provides Azure Web PubSub setup, client usage, groups, tokens, permissions, and error handling.
actual_capabilities: Shows the Maven dependency for com.azure:azure-messaging-webpubsub version 1.5.0.
Demonstrates service client creation with connection strings, access keys, DefaultAzureCredential, and async clients.
Shows how to send messages to all clients, groups, users, and specific connections.
Covers group membership, connection management, and user presence checks.
Demonstrates client access token generation, roles, group scopes, and permissions.
Includes environment variable placeholders and basic HttpResponseException handling.
limitations: It does not create Azure resources or configure Web PubSub service settings.
It does not provide a complete runnable application or automated tests.
Examples require secure replacement of placeholders before use in production.
It may not cover SDK changes released after the documented examples.

use_cases.title: Add Live Notifications
use_cases.description: Implement server-to-client push notifications in a Java backend using Azure Web PubSub send patterns.

use_cases.title: Manage Real-Time Groups
use_cases.description: Use group and user APIs to route chat, collaboration, or dashboard updates to the right connections.

use_cases.title: Review Access Patterns
use_cases.description: Plan token generation, role assignment, permission checks, and credential handling for a real-time service.

prompt_templates.title: Add the Java Dependency
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me add Azure Web PubSub to a Java Maven project and explain which dependency version this skill documents.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Service Client
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to create an Azure Web PubSub service client in Java using secure configuration values.

prompt_templates.title: Design Group Messaging
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design Java Web PubSub group messaging for a chat feature with users, groups, and targeted broadcasts.

prompt_templates.title: Review Token Permissions
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Azure Web PubSub token and permission flow for least privilege, safe expiration, and log-safe handling.

output_examples.input: Need a Java backend that broadcasts outage alerts to connected clients.
output_examples.output: A concise plan covering client creation, send-to-all usage, content type selection, and error handling checks.

output_examples.input: Need chat rooms with different permissions for members and moderators.
output_examples.output: A group-based design that separates rooms, assigns scoped roles, and avoids broad permissions where possible.

output_examples.input: Need to troubleshoot failed Web PubSub sends from a Java service.
output_examples.output: A debugging checklist covering endpoint configuration, hub name, credential source, exception status, and target connection state.

best_practices: Store connection strings, endpoints, and access keys in secure configuration, not source files.
Use short token lifetimes and grant only the roles each client needs.
Prefer scoped groups and hubs to keep real-time traffic isolated by feature or tenant.
anti_patterns: Do not log generated client access URLs or tokens.
Do not grant broad join or send roles when group-specific roles are enough.
Do not hardcode Azure endpoints, connection strings, or access keys in application code.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps build Java services that use Azure Web PubSub for WebSocket messaging and live updates.

faq.question: Does it include async Java examples?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes async client creation and async send examples using subscription callbacks.

faq.question: Can it help with group messaging?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers sending to groups, adding connections or users to groups, and checking membership.

faq.question: Does it create Azure resources?
faq.answer: No. You must create and configure the Azure Web PubSub resource outside this skill.

faq.question: How should credentials be handled?
faq.answer: Use secure configuration or managed identity when possible. Avoid hardcoding secrets in source code.

faq.question: Is it suitable for production security design?
faq.answer: It provides useful patterns, but production systems need a separate review of authentication, authorization, logging, and monitoring.
